touches.text: The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.

The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. - CC

Three instrument runs at once share the repo, /tmp, the network and git, so a red can come from a neighbour. HYPOTHESIS: a red is re-run once, alone, before it is recorded; both readings stand on the verdict, and a red that turns green alone is a contention red. Its WATCHME brings cc_0 every re-run's pair of readings, so the hypothesis is reviewed against them (0.6.1). - CC

An instrument is the literal command the sealer runs, never prose about how to run one. Why? The verdict must come from a hand the builder did not guide (9.4.2.2), and prose needs a reader to guess the command; validate moves to deterministic code (9.3.2.1). CC's decision, Q#126, on "we are moving away from prose ... we need things we can check" -amm. - CC

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

Each stage moves from the model to deterministic code once a proof a hollow build could not pass can hold it; hypothesize stays with the model longest. Validate sends a local miss back to hypothesize and a structural one back to design. A build that finds new work spawns children that enter at decompose.
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal.
Weekly: what is too long or too host-bound to run daily, such as hollow re-runs of every proof and each box's own run of the proofs it can run.

One bus per cairn instance, not per host. Each box runs its own bus, and the buses talk to one another, so a device always talks to the bus on its own box; together they are the instance's one bus. A device runs on one box; the other boxes reach it over the buses. No box needs a full set of devices. WHY: so the instance can run several heavy tasks at once across boxes.
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
A proof that cannot go red without its build (its hollow is empty) stands only on Akien's answered approval, recorded as the hollow reading and re-read at clearance; any other empty hollow is red.

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
Scratch bus: a proof needs a bus it controls (a real store, stub devices, nobody live listening), so the cairn device publishes scratch_bus, the way db_domain's client carries scratch().
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).
